quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move into the left lane. You should:

options.text: Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot.
Look in your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: As you enter an intersection, the traffic light turns yellow. You should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Carefully drive through the intersection.
questions.explanation: Yellow means slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely, you may drive through carefully.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop at least 15 feet from the railroad tracks when you see flashing signals. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or sounds of a train approaching.

questions.question: If two vehicles reach an unmarked intersection at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left.
The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
One driver should demand the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked intersection, the driver on the left must let the driver on the right go first. Do not assume another driver will give you the right-of-way.

questions.question: To stay safe while driving in bad weather, you should:

options.text: Leave more space between you and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Worn tires do not grip the road well when it is wet. Drive with good tires, increase your following distance, and reduce your speed in poor weather.

questions.question: Your license will be suspended if you get ____ points in 12 months.
questions.correctAnswerText: 12 or more
questions.explanation: Points are added to your record when you get a traffic ticket. If you get 12 or more points in 12 months, your license will be suspended or revoked.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to finish a left turn. You should:

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get other drivers to let you through.
Drive around the back of a car that is blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. This way, if another car hits you from behind, you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Stop and go when it is safe.
Stop. Do not turn in the direction of the arrow until it turns green.
Turn slowly in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop. Do not turn in the direction of the arrow until it turns green.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means stop. Do not turn in that direction. Wait until the arrow turns green or becomes a flashing yellow arrow before you turn.

questions.question: Parking lights may only be used:

options.text: When it is hard to see.
Within one hour of sunset or sunrise.
When driving below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a vehicle is parked.
questions.explanation: Use parking lights only when your vehicle is parked and not moving.

questions.question: The speed limit on most Alaska roads is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: Business districts, alleys, school zones, and residential areas have their own speed limits. All other roads in Alaska have a 55 mph speed limit unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is coming. The road splits into two separate one-way lanes with a median between them. You must stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What makes a good defensive driver?

options.text: Watches for what other drivers do.
Drives at the same speed all the time.
Only drives in places they know.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches for what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers can get distracted. A defensive driver watches for what other drivers do and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: What do statistics show about alcohol in car crashes?

options.text: Alcohol is involved in almost half of all fatal car crashes.
Alcohol is rarely involved in car crashes.
Alcohol is only in crashes that do not cause deaths.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol is involved in almost half of all fatal car crashes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol plays a major role in deadly car crashes. Almost 45 percent of all traffic deaths each year involve alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use the brakes right away.
Slowly slow down and pull to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and do not brake right away. Slowly reduce speed and gently apply the brakes before pulling off the side of the road.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus dropping off children, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking on the side of the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: When you see a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when can you pass?

options.text: When the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, and the broken line is on your side, you can pass if no cars are coming toward you.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when changing lanes?

options.text: Look for other drivers in the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers. Look for other drivers moving into the same lane. Never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: It is illegal to park within ____ of a fire hydrant.
questions.correctAnswerText: 15 feet
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: Switch to low beam headlights when you are within ____ of an oncoming car.
questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet
questions.explanation: Bright headlights from oncoming cars can make your eyes contract and reduce your vision. When driving at night, switch to low beams within 500 feet of oncoming traffic to protect other drivers.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear to be drunk. Opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert.
